races.name: Burke's Clonbur 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's hold-up type has flat form only (best of 5th) and this is a first hurdle start — De Bromhead's hurdling debut runners are always of interest, but the hold-up style may leave her dependent on a fast pace that Montevetro is unlikely to generate; Strand top pick at low confidence.

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's runner won on the AW at Dundalk and is a natural hold-up operator, but with the rear of the field likely congested by several similar types, she will probably race in midfield rather than from her ideal rearward berth, blunting the effectiveness of her customary late challenge.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's prominent racer has shown consistency in bumpers including a 4th over this sort of trip and the prominent style suits this race shape perfectly — gets to sit just off Montevetro and track the gallop throughout, T14 at 2/36 tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's mare is the form pick among the prominent types — a hurdle winner on soft at Cork brings proven jumping ability, and the tongue-tie is already applied; sits in a favourable tactical position to track the leader and has the best winning form of the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's 3yo has only a single run to go on — a 4th over 18f — and while the midfield style is mapped appropriately, the lightly raced profile means significant unknowns remain; Thomas O'Connor (7) takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Armillary
runners_data.note: Tara Lee Cogan's debutant is completely unknown — no racing history, unlisted jockey profile, style tagged as Unknown; treat as a wild card whose contribution to the race shape cannot be assessed.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's runner holds hold-up form over longer trips but has pulled up in a point and managed only an 8th on hurdle debut — his natural rearward style is likely squeezed into midfield in a large-field scenario, with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflecting the mismatch; Josh Younge (7) rides.

runners_data.name: Step By Step
runners_data.note: Aidan Howard's hurdling debutant carries headgear (h) from the outset and is entirely unknown on form — the Unknown style tag and absence of any race history makes this one of the bigger puzzles in the field.

runners_data.name: Wills History
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's debutant has no visible form record and an Unknown style classification; the yard sends only occasional runners and the lack of any history makes a meaningful assessment impossible.

runners_data.name: We're Out Of Aces
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's unknown debutant is the most interesting blank slate in the field — Elliott's T14 of 4/33 is a strong trainer angle and his hurdling debuts often outrun their prices, but without a style tag or form string the race shape impact is unquantifiable.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: R P Cody's hold-up type has a modest flat and hurdle record and is another genuine hold-up runner likely to find the rear congested — with a STYLE_FIT of 0.93, the note here is that his best-case run emerges only if a strong pace string the field out; Paddy Cody (7) takes the ride for the family yard.

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's front-runner is the key pace figure — confirmed as the sole leader, placed twice on the AW, and stepping up in trip to 2m2f which could suit; the uncontested lead on Good to Yielding is a genuine asset and his price deserves respect in light of that tactical control.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Cromwell's hold-up type has been placed once in 7 runs and worn headgear (h) throughout; finished 2nd over 10f on Good which shows ability, but recent runs have been modest and the hold-up profile does not suit the anticipated race shape.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up runner (no jockey confirmed) has placed twice from 5 runs over a variety of trips — the step up in trip to 2m2f could bring improvement but the hold-up style puts him in competition with several other rear-of-field types for limited room.

runners_data.name: Matada
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up runner returns after 111 days off — the long layoff is a notable flag on what is her first hurdle start, and all three flat runs produced low finishes (11th-14th range); conditions are fine but the profile is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's blinkers-wearing hold-up runner has been consistently mid-division or worse across six flat runs, all on Good; the headgear switch to blinkers may sharpen him but the form line is flat and 6 days since last run is an unusual quick turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Montevetro is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse field and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead from the off, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over 2m2f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. That lone-leader scenario creates a relatively compressed race shape through the early and middle stages, with the prominent types — Chairmanforlife and Misty Cove — likely to sit closest in behind and apply the first pressure at the business end. This field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too, and Another Day Done are genuine hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield pocket rather than enjoying a clean passage from the rear, which materially compromises their chance of delivering a late run. With Montevetro able to control fractions and the prominent/handy runners gifted a clean sight of him throughout, this race shape strongly favours horses racing close to the pace who can travel smoothly and pick off the leader in the straight — a patient but positionally-comfortable prominent style is the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Montevetro Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent horses travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Montevetro dictates from flag to finish at a pace that suits those travelling just off his shoulder, and the closest pursuers — Chairmanforlife, Misty Cove — are best placed to strike when the gallop quickens from two out. Horses held up have too much ground to make up and risk being caught in traffic in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro sets fractions steady enough that no rival can reel him in and he stays on strongly to the line.
scenarios.body: Montevetro, untroubled throughout, gets a breather mid-race on the long Ballinrobe circuit and finds enough in reserve to repel the closers in the straight; his form shows a placed effort at flat tracks and a step up in trip could bring improvement. The prominent horses fail to produce the turn of foot needed to overhaul a horse who has dictated on his own terms.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front group ties each other up, giving genuine hold-up runners late momentum.
scenarios.body: Divine Believer, as the Strand Scorecard selection, holds a realistic chance here if stamina is the determining factor in the closing stages and traffic clears in time. Another Day Done and Camp Verde are true hold-up types but are tagged as redistributed — meaning they will likely be trapped in midfield rather than getting a clean run from the rear, limiting their ability to produce the expected late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches, pace collapses mid-race, and a late surge off a truly muddling gallop becomes decisive.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn race on Good to Yielding ground with 16 runners and a lone front-runner can occasionally unravel into a messy sprint finish where unexposed horses with unknown profiles benefit; Armillary, Step By Step, and We're Out Of Aces are complete unknowns who could capitalise on a muddled shape. Probability is low as Montevetro's control is the dominant expectation, but the size of the field keeps a chaotic outcome in play.

watchPoints.text: Misty Cove is the most dangerous prominent runner — a proven hurdle winner with headgear already applied, travelling in the ideal position just off Montevetro; if she jumps cleanly on the first circuit she is best placed of all to land a telling blow in the straight.

The redistributed trio of Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too, and Another Day Done are all genuine hold-up types likely to find themselves in a congested midfield with nowhere to go — watch for trouble-in-running incidents between them as they compete for the same patch of ground from the 1m mark.

We're Out Of Aces (Gordon Elliott, T14 4/33) is a completely unknown debutant from a powerful yard that hits at a solid strike rate — without a style tag, this runner could surface from anywhere in the field and should not be ignored at big odds.

Montevetro's ability to control the fractions entirely unchallenged is the single biggest variable in the race — if he is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip the entire shape is settled; only watch for an early challenge from Chairmanforlife or Misty Cove that might push the pace higher than expected.

Matada's 111-day absence and moderate flat form makes her one to monitor early — if she jumps poorly or gets outpaced in the first half mile she will take no further part in the contest, but any significant drift in the market beforehand would be worth noting given the Cromwell yard.

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's consistent filly has three places from five hurdle starts on similar going — she's a natural front-runner whose true style means she'll press to get forward despite the midfield map position, and that effort to secure a berth may not come for free over 2m2f.

runners_data.name: The Dotski
runners_data.note: Henry de Bromhead runner returning after 195 days off having shown modest form on Flat-style hurdle tracks; needs to find significant improvement on debut hurdle form and the layoff is a legitimate concern.

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 5yo has a win and two places in four hurdle starts, all on good-ish ground, and carries 161lbs; her natural style pushes her forward but the crowded prominent group means she'll need to work to hold that position, which the weight won't help.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: Placed second in a 2m3f maiden hurdle on good ground and holds an OR of 97 — a legitimate prominent type with no redistribution concern, Richard Deegan takes the ride and the step back to 2m2f from 2m3f is fine.

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: Has six placings without a win and the form string shows consistent mid-division finishes around 2m; apprentice Ross Berry aboard and the trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days, making it hard to read yard form.

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Last seen finishing pulled-up on good to soft in May and has had 88 days off; hold-up style suits the projected race shape in theory but the form figures show a horse in steep decline.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins trained and only two hurdle runs to assess — fell on debut then fourth; a natural prominent type crammed into a bigger field than she's faced, and without a jockey named, confidence in her status is limited.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Mullins runner with an OR of 104 and placed twice from four hurdle runs; travels prominently and has shown enough over 2m2f on good ground to be live if she secures a clean run — the apprentice Sean Cleary-Farrell is the query.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: An 8yo with a modest recent form string including hurdle pulls-up; sits naturally in midfield and one fourth place on good ground is her sole recent positive — tough ask in this company.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Six and sevens tell the story — three hurdle runs and never closer than sixth; no jockey named and trainer Darren Collins has had only two runners in the past fortnight, not an obvious threat.

runners_data.name: Tara Boe
runners_data.note: An 8yo hurdler whose sole recent start produced an eighth over 2m on good ground; hard to see how she improves enough here on the step back to a field of this size.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Twice placed third in hurdles on good ground and stays well enough on the evidence of form at 2m2f; consistent without threatening to win, and John Paul O'Hanlon has ridden her before.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with one second and a fall in the last five runs; Tom Kelly (7) takes the ride and the 2m2f trip on good to yielding looks within range for a horse who placed at 2m on good.

runners_data.name: Mia In Milan
runners_data.note: Three starts and a best of fifth on good ground; hold-up style suits the race shape theoretically but form figures offer nothing to suggest she can capitalise from 94 days off.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Alexy
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner returning after 251 days off — she finished third on heavy ground before the break and her front-running style gives her a soft lead here, though the layoff and modest form mean her role may be more tempo-setter than winner.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Two ninths in hurdles on good ground tell their own story; midfield type with no jockey confirmed and a trainer without recent runners — little to recommend her.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly's 4yo has placed twice in three hurdle runs on similar going, including a second on soft; hold-up style suits the projected race shape, Peter Smithers (5) keeps the ride, and the trainer has had two winners from 12 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: Five career hurdle runs yielding four places and consistent form in the 3-5 range over 2m-2m2f on good ground — John Patrick Ryan's hold-up filly is rock-solid without quite winning and suits the projected late-run shape.

races.paceDynamic: Kilbarry Alexy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner mares' maiden hurdle and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she is set to control tempo from the front on Good to Yielding ground over 2m2f — a pace that is sustainable rather than searching. The prominent cluster is overcrowded: Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, and Katie Can't Count are all natural front-to-prominent types who will be squeezed into a midfield berth by sheer weight of numbers, meaning Kilbarry Alexy effectively gets a soft lead with Rosarian, The Dotski, and Ronnie's Rascal filling the seats immediately behind. With a lone pace-setter dictating at a measured clip over a trip that stretches stamina on easy ground, the race shape heavily favours horses who travel with cover in midfield or hold-up positions and pick up once the early pace softens in the final half-mile — genuine closers who relish this ground and trip will be best served. The field holds more prominent types than can realistically secure a forward berth; of those redistributed, Brave Lady has the strongest credentials and profile to muscle forward from the gate, with Goodgollymissholly also capable but less certain to get the position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the race only quickens from the second-last, allowing hold-up horses to deliver a measured late challenge.
scenarios.body: With the pace genuinely sustainable, hold-up runners travelling under cover will arrive full of running at the business end, and the Good to Yielding surface rewards those who save energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Brave Lady Fronts Up
scenarios.trigger: If Brave Lady overcomes redistribution and forces her way to a prominent position early, dictating or co-dictating with Kilbarry Alexy.
scenarios.body: A genuine prominent type with strong placed form in similar going, Brave Lady's 0W3P profile flatters her consistency and she would relish a comfort blanket of a lead rather than racing off the pace she's been forced to sit off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Suit Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sooner than expected through the final circuit and the race becomes an attritional test of stamina on the softening ground.
scenarios.body: Horses with strong staying profiles and proven form over 2m2f+ on soft-ish ground will grind out the others, with the distance stretching out those who travel prominently but fade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group causes early shuffling that compromises hold-up horses and a prominent type slips the field turning for home.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic scenario where closers lose ground at a crucial stage, a prominent runner with a clean passage benefits from the resulting gaps.

watchPoints.text: Brave Lady is likely to push forward aggressively from the gate despite her midfield map placement — watch the first two furlongs to see if she secures a prominent berth, which would meaningfully upgrade her chance.

With Goodgollymissholly (161lbs) and Katie Can't Count also trying to press forward, the first bend with 18 runners on a tight track like Ballinrobe is a genuine traffic flashpoint — any incident there could compromise several runners simultaneously.

Kilbarry Alexy returns after 251 days off for a yard with no recent recorded runners — if she gets tired mid-race and drops away sharply, the tempo could collapse in a way that makes the race tactical and unpredictable from the second-last.

Mastertown Miss is the Strand Scorecard top selection at medium confidence — watch whether Peter Smithers (5) gets a clean passage in the hold-up group; if she gets boxed in behind traffic turning for home her chance evaporates quickly in a field this size.

Ronnie's Rascal (OR 104, highest rated in the field) may be the most significant market mover to watch at the off — if punted significantly it would signal stable confidence that the apprentice booking is not a concern and she is ready to step forward.

runners_data.name: Take The Free
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer with strong recent form including a win at 20f on Good; trainer Bolger has a live 14-day record and 67-day absence is acceptable, but 156lbs and a 4-year-old taking on older rivals at this trip requires scrutiny.
runners_data.comment: Ran to winning effect most recently and has going experience to call on, but a lengthy 67-day absence is a notable query and he carries 156 lb against a competitive field; that layoff makes him harder to place with confidence.

runners_data.name: Crossing The Bar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced warning flags everywhere — 523 days absent, unknown going profile, and a handler with a modest recent strike rate; the hg:t tongue-tie notation adds intrigue but this is a horse requiring a significant leap of faith on fitness grounds.
runners_data.comment: Crossing The Bar showed a fine turn of foot when winning three starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions to back up a rating of 118, making him a genuine danger; the sole concern is whether a 523-day absence leaves him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style performer with a win over 18f on Good and placed efforts at 20f and 24f; Noel Meade yard is ticking along at 1/32 over 14 days which is modest, but the horse's own form figures on similar going (1W2P from three) are genuinely competitive.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures and with his trainer in wretched form at 1/32 over the past fortnight, Mickey Cohen is hard to fancy despite a win three starts back; fourth last time out after 61 days off makes the return uncertain too.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who won over 20f on Good and finished second over this identical 26f trip; a 5lb claimer handles him and the trainer's 14-day blank (0/2) is a minor concern, but a 23-day turnaround and proven form at the distance make him interesting.
runners_data.comment: Ran well last time out with a second, and a winner two starts back, but that seventh three starts back tempers expectations; has run over today's trip and going, and 157 lb is a stern test for a gelding ranked mid-field here.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Dangers-listed hold-up type who has placed twice at 22f on Good and handles this going well; the 5lb claiming rider Alan O'Sullivan reduces the weight burden and a 20-day fresher run adds energy, though the trainer's 0/3 over 14 days is unremarkable.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, Jupiter Du Gite has finished second in each of his last two outings and has run over today's trip and going, giving him every chance to go one better here; he carries 162 lb but our rating of 129, top of these, makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Better Times
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style whose most recent form includes a win over 22f on Soft; 104 days off the track is a moderate concern and the card has pushed this horse into a midfield mapping — its natural position is from the rear, which may prove hard to hold on a compressed field, tempering the chance if the race lacks a strong gallop.
runners_data.comment: Better Times has experience of today's distance and going, and a win features in his recent starts, but he was last seen finishing seventh and has been off the track for 104 days; 155 lb is no help either.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; blinkered, with a course win over 26f on Good, but the yard's 0/38 over 14 days for Gavin Cromwell is a stark stat and a 7lb apprentice riding him to dictate terms adds execution risk on a tricky course.
runners_data.comment: Mr Dibbs won three starts back but has since finished eighth and sixth, and with his trainer yet to strike from 38 attempts in the past fortnight and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, he faces a stiff task despite going experience and a return after just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: Consistent wide-of-the-mark finisher in seven recent hurdle starts with zero wins or places on Good in that span; a true hold-up type placed midfield on the pace map due to field congestion, and the form record does not inspire confidence regardless of scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, Strange Currency faces a stiff ask on these figures — ranked 13 of 14 — though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 32-day break carrying 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: Top-rated selection on the Strand Scorecard racing as a hold-up type; ten-year-old with a recent win over 20f on Good and a placed effort at 18f, blinkers fitted, and Cromwell's Arcland shows a sharper profile than stablemate Mr Dibbs — 15 days since last run is fine and the Good to Yielding suits given the going history.
runners_data.comment: Arcland won two starts back and was second three starts back, showing a consistent profile over today's going, and his 15-day turnaround looks spot on; the main concern is a trainer who has drawn a blank in 38 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR=121 but the form string ends in a pull-up and the yard has not fired a winner in 14 days; prominent-style horse whose 167lbs topweight is a serious impost and the hist shows limited fire on today's going variant across 13 relevant runs.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in his last five starts — third three starts back and second four starts back — Ehteyat rates a serious threat here off a 22-day break, our rating of 123 putting him second of 14; the main concern is that pulled-up latest effort.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: Returned just seven days ago and the short turnaround for a hold-up horse who has not finished in the frame in five recent runs is a red flag; naturally a closer by trade, the pace map places this horse in midfield by necessity, and the form — 0W0P from nine similar-going runs — does not encourage.
runners_data.comment: Free Flow has run over today's going and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround, but he has been winless in his last five starts, his recent efforts including a fourth and a sixth, and our rating of 110 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 97 implies.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Young hold-up performer whose two wins have both come over shorter trips; placed third over 20f on Good most recently and OR=116 at age four suggests unexposed potential, but 23 days between runs and a tricky field position to navigate in a 14-runner field are the key variables.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, In The Minus arrives on the back of reasonable form and has run over today's going before, though a hefty 159 lb burden and a ranking of sixth from fourteen in the field are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: Dangers-listed by the Strand with back-to-back placed efforts at 22f and 24f on Good — exactly the profile this trip rewards; a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping by field congestion, but the 3lb claimer Shane O'Callaghan has live credentials and a trainer firing at 1/26 over 14 days gives context.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last of the 14 on our figures, Pilgrims Walk faces a stiff task under 140 lb, with his trainer in poor form at 1/26 over the past fortnight; experience over today's trip and going offers some small crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Needs Must
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard is in excellent 14-day form (4/33) and the horse won over 20f on Soft, which is the most relevant going precedent; 178 days off the track is the elephant in the room for a prominent-style runner who has not raced since before Christmas, and the pulled-up run on the Flat before that layoff adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Needs Must landed a win three starts back but has since fallen and finished unplaced, leaving his form hard to read; 178 days off the track adds further uncertainty, though he carries a competitive weight and his rating of 118 keeps him respected here.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Dibbs is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful rival likely to dispute the lead from flag to finish, he should control the tempo from the front at a pace dictated entirely on his own terms over 2m6f of Good to Yielding ground. Take The Free, Mickey Cohen, and Ehteyat are genuine prominent types who will track closely behind, ensuring the race is run at a workmanlike but not suicidal gallop — steady enough to set it up for those in behind but not so slow as to create a pure sprint finish. The field contains a glut of hold-up horses — Better Times, Strange Currency, Free Flow, and Pilgrims Walk are all true closers who have been mapped to midfield because there is insufficient room at the rear for all of them to race in their natural position; of these, Pilgrims Walk and Better Times are most likely to actually secure a workable tracking berth given their recent proximity form. With one genuine front-runner dictating a sustainable pace and a congested chasing pack, this race shape strongly favours patient hold-up types who can travel through the race travelling well and produce a clean late run — horses racing from a genuine off-the-pace position over this stamina test on softening ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arcland Leads Hold-Up Charge
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs sets a controlled solo tempo and true hold-up runners can navigate clear runs from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs rolls along unchallenged through the early and middle stages while the prominent trio of Take The Free, Mickey Cohen, and Ehteyat absorb minor pressure, leaving genuine closers to hunt them down from two out; on Good to Yielding ground over 2m6f the stamina test is real and those who switch off early and finish strongly have the clearest edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that those racing prominently never get seriously tested and the hold-up horses find the gaps closing before the last.
scenarios.body: Take The Free or Mickey Cohen travel comfortably in the slipstream of Mr Dibbs and, if the tempo is modest, kick on approaching the last before the closers can mount a serious challenge; at 2m6f on this going a somnambulant pace is unlikely but a moderate gallop would suit those able to race closer to the action throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs is ridden more aggressively than expected or prominent types push the pace, creating a true test of stamina in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop would drain the prominent pack and open the race right up for any hold-up horse with a clear passage; on softening ground the stamina angle becomes decisive and those who have shown ability to finish off races over big distances would land in the money.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that Mr Dibbs or a prominent companion is never put under pressure and steals the race on a loose lead.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs, having set his own fractions and never been seriously headed, finds enough reserves to hold on as closers fail to bridge the gap in time; this outcome requires the chasing pack to misjudge the race entirely but a 7lb claimer on a front-runner with modest opposition is not impossible.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mr Dibbs closely in the early stages — if apprentice Alix Balfe (7lb) is unable to control the early fractions, a truly contentious tempo could dramatically alter the race shape and blow open the hold-up scenario.

Arcland carries blinkers and is trained by Cromwell, whose stable is running at 0/38 over 14 days — monitor the market; if the money doesn't come for the selection, the cold trainer form is a real dampener on confidence.

Needs Must represents the Gordon Elliott yard who are flying at 4/33 over 14 days, but 178 days off the track for a prominent type stepping back up in trip is a significant fitness question — watch the opening exchanges to assess freshness.

Better Times and Strange Currency are both flagged as redistributed hold-up horses who may struggle to find their natural position in this congested 14-runner field — if either is seen pulling early or racing out of character, their chance deflates sharply.

Crossing The Bar is 523 days absent and fitted with a tongue-tie — watch the pre-race paddock behaviour and early movement carefully, as any sluggishness or greenness returning from such a layoff would effectively eliminate this runner from contention.

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong Good ground form (sim-going 6/6, 1W3P) and De Bromhead stable; STYLE_FIT flag notes she is racing somewhat out of her most natural role, so watch for whether she truly controls or merely leads by default — key horse for the race shape regardless.
runners_data.comment: Cobra Queen arrives here in solid heart after back-to-back thirds, and with experience of today's trip and going she appeals as the one to beat off 166 lb, though she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: McConnell-trained six-year-old who races prominently and returns after 16 days; good ground record but zero wins and no places in five runs on sim going limits confidence, and the step up in trip to 2m6f is untested in her recent form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Camlin Park nonetheless catches the eye on going and distance experience, and our rating of 116 suggests she is better than her official mark of 109; the chief concern is a recent string of disappointing efforts, including two pull-ups.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with four places in recent similar-going runs (sim-going 6/10, 0W4P); the nine-year-old handles this trip and surface well and will sit handy throughout, making her a reliable each-way threat if Cobra Queen tires.
runners_data.comment: Theflyingbee has been remarkably consistent, finishing second twice and third twice in her last four starts, and our rating of 124 marks her out as a serious threat here; the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won over 2m2f on Good ground last time and is versatile enough to race from midfield; Ross O'Sullivan yard in modest recent form (T14: 1/13) and the 7lb claimer Shane Markey is a factor, but the step to 2m6f on softer ground is the key query.
runners_data.comment: Walkingmayotomilan won last time out but that single success punctuates a largely disappointing recent record of unplaced runs and a pull-up, and our rating has her a clear last of eleven in this field; she has run over today's distance and going, and the 32-day break at least means she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who handles this trip and ground well (1W3P in sim going), and scored at 2m4f on Good; racing prominently under Kevin Sexton, she arrives 38 days fresh and is the most credible established rival to Cobra Queen on form.
runners_data.comment: Sound Judgement won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing she can mix it at this level, but a sixth last time out after 38 days off raises a fitness query; the 153 lb burden is a stiff ask as she drops back into midfield contention.

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won over 2m2f on Good ground but has run poorly since (7th, 7th); trainer McLoughlin at 1/2 in 14-day window suggests rare but possible form, yet the horse's recent record makes it hard to trust from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Nothing Hectic won last time out and also took a win five starts back, but the two seventh-place finishes and a pulled up in between temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and going, and 152 lb is a stern test of whether she can sustain that recent upturn.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: Absent 345 days — the longest layoff in the field — and showed little in her only sim-going run; the fade-in-finish flag is a significant concern, and returning from near a year off in a competitive mares' handicap hurdle over 2m6f is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for nearly a year, St Anthonys Corner faces a stiff ask here, ranked 10 of 11 on our figures despite carrying 140 lb; experience over today's trip and going offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer (hist: multiple top-three finishes from the rear) whose natural closing position is compromised here — placed in midfield on the map due to the volume of rear-runners, so she may not get the clean late run her style demands; STYLE_FIT flag appropriately tempers her chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Run For The Border makes it hard to build a case; that said, she returns quickly on 11 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going before, and her third two starts back shows she can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard top selection, though rated low confidence; her genuine hold-up style (REDISTRIBUTED) means she may race closer than ideal in this traffic-heavy shape, and the 7lb claimer Sean Cleary-Farrell faces a stiff ask getting her into contention from a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last four starts — third last time out, and a winner five starts back — You Make Me Smile arrives on familiar going after a 36-day break, though 146 lb is a stern burden and an eighth-of-eleven ranking suggests she faces stiffer opposition here.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a place last time at 2m2f; Gibney yard quiet (T14: 0/4) and the horse has never won, but consistent placed form on Good ground and ability to finish off a strong pace gives her some each-way relevance if the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Bossy Bird shaped with promise when second three starts back, but she has drifted out of the frame in both outings since and remains winless in her last five starts; the 150 lb burden is a further ask, even if she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: In-form mare who has won her last two starts (1/24f SOF, 1/22f GOO) and handles both Good and Soft ground well; racing from hold-up position under amateur Mr E M Nugent, she brings the most recent winning form in the race and demands respect as a dark horse.
runners_data.comment: She'll Be Kept arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; the main question is whether 160 lb blunts her momentum after 38 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Cobra Queen is the confirmed front-runner and should set a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good to Yielding ground, with no natural rival prepared to challenge her for the lead. Sound Judgement, Camlin Park and Theflyingbee are all prominent types who will press for early position behind her, creating a reasonably honest early tempo that should stretch the field out on Ballinrobe's undulating track. This field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate cleanly — You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border are genuine hold-up horses who may find themselves racing closer than ideal given the clustering of midfield traffic, while Cobra Queen herself carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she is racing somewhat out of role at the head of affairs. The resulting shape — a single uncontested leader, compressed midfield — will favour prominent-to-mid horses with proven stamina at this trip and the class to pick up at the business end, rather than true closers who may find the pace too honest to generate a late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cobra Queen controls throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged and the prominent horses behind fail to close the gap turning in.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen dictates a measured gallop, the Sound Judgement/Theflyingbee group track her at a respectful distance but cannot sustain their effort on the run-in after the stiff 2m6f on yielding ground; the front-runner's class and prominent rivals' inability to quicken leaves the initiative with the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent stalker pounces late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent tracking horses — Sound Judgement or Theflyingbee — sits a length off Cobra Queen and produces a decisive jump at the last.
scenarios.body: The steady early gallop set by Cobra Queen preserves enough for a well-placed tracker to pounce in the straight, with the trip and going suiting a horse who has been hunting the leader from close range; Sound Judgement's proven stamina at 2m4f-plus and Elliott stable form makes her the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse finishes powerfully
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a sustained finish and a late runner bursts through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: She'll Be Kept, who has won her last two starts and arrives in form, or Bossy Bird could emerge from the rear if the field strings out and leaves a clear passage; however, You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border carry redistribution flags meaning their natural closing style is compromised by likely midrace positioning, limiting the probability of a pure late flourish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — pace collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen's effort unexpectedly fades early and the race becomes a messy, slowly-run scramble with the field bunched.
scenarios.body: A false pace would suit a horse with a sharp turn of foot who can sprint in the closing stages; Walkingmayotomilan's recent win form and midfield position gives her a route through, while Nothing Hectic would be best placed of the hold-up brigade if the tempo drops away dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Cobra Queen's grip on the lead is everything — if she is challenged early by Sound Judgement or Camlin Park pressing for position, the race shape shifts from controlled to contested and all probabilities reset.

She'll Be Kept arrives on a two-timer and her form is markedly better than her OR of 112 suggests; if Mr Nugent can navigate clear of midfield traffic, she could be the biggest danger to the front-runners late on.

You Make Me Smile (Strand top, low confidence) is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution — watch whether Cleary-Farrell (7lb claimer) is able to place her in a realistic striking position or whether she gets buried in traffic.

Good to Yielding ground prevails across the entire Ballinrobe card, confirming no meaningful going upgrade expected — horses with proven form on this surface (Cobra Queen 6/6, Theflyingbee 6/10) hold a factual edge over those with only a few sim-going runs.

St Anthonys Corner's 345-day absence combined with the fade-in-finish flag makes her a significant drifter of resources in any pace model — monitor her early race movement; if she is prominent early she is likely to compromise others' runs when weakening.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: OR 122 gives her a class edge in a beginners' chase; Carl Millar (5) partnered her in recent form and she's been placed in all three runs on similar going, making her the natural controlling force here at 6yo.
runners_data.comment: Affinity Rock arrives in fine fettle after a sequence of three consecutive placings, including second two starts back and third last time out, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that 161 lb is a sizeable burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Carried With Love
runners_data.note: 222 days off the track is the headline flag — long absence into a beginners' chase against fresher rivals; naturally wants to race up with the pace but the congested prominent group means she's likely to find herself further back than suits, tempering confidence.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter who has finished third on three occasions in recent starts, with a second one start back showcasing her best, though she returns after 222 days off and carries a hefty 161 lb; has experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 127 makes her the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Straight Home
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner with only one chase start on record (placed on Good) and a form string that includes a win, making her respect-worthy on trainer alone; Cleary-Farrell's 7lb claim is a small bonus, but limited chase history means jumping fluency is an open question over 2m7f.
runners_data.comment: Straight Home won two of her last four starts and brings solid recent form into this, having run over today's trip and going; the chief concern is whether 161 lb proves too stiff an impost against a strong field.

runners_data.name: Cooke's Lass
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott handler lends obvious credence, but she's 364 days between runs and has a pull-up on her recent form card; hold-up style means she needs the race to fall apart in front of her, which is plausible but not the dominant shape here.
runners_data.comment: Cooke's Lass returns after a 364-day absence carrying 161 lb, and her recent form — pulled up last time, a fall three starts back, and a second before that — gives a mixed picture; going experience helps, but she's winless in her last four starts and fitness on comeback day is the key query.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Five runs on Good ground with a best of third tells a consistent but non-winning story; Emmet Mullins sends her in with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, suggesting the yard is trying to find more from her, but she's been placed without winning in this grade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Giorgia Rose makes little appeal at the weights carrying 161 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and those three consecutive third-place finishes one, two and three starts back hint at a degree of consistency.

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: Two wins from nine runs on Good ground and strong course familiarity make her one of the more interesting prominent types; Alix Balfe's 7lb claim could be a booking to note, and her form string (1,3,1,6,1) shows she can produce on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back, Joya Del Mar has run over today's trip and going and returns after 33 days, but a fifth last time out and a ranking of sixth in this field of nine on our rating suggest she faces a stiff task under 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: OR 104 and a win on Good over 2m4f in his history; hold-up style leaves him dependent on traffic clearing, and two P finishes in recent form suggest he's not at his sharpest, though John Patrick Ryan's yard has had recent runners.
runners_data.comment: Twice pulled up in her last two starts is the obvious concern, but Ad Caelum showed her quality with a win earlier in this recent sequence, and she arrives on a fair turnaround of 21 days, with experience of today's distance and going and a our rating of 114 lending substance to her claims.

runners_data.name: Cherry Red
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good going and returned a placed effort; naturally prominent but pushed wide of that position by the field's pace dynamics, meaning he'll need to work harder to get competitive — discount his chance accordingly given he's racing out of his ideal role.
runners_data.comment: Cherry Red arrives having been unplaced last time out after a win the start before, and with a pulled up and an unseated also in recent starts, consistency is a real concern; rated lowest of the nine runners, she faces a stiff task off 161 lb, though she does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Survivors Sister
runners_data.note: OR 102 and a win within the last five starts; Philip Donovan takes the ride for Paul John Gilligan's yard, and although 108 days off the track requires a fitness tick, her form on Good going includes two placed efforts over a range of distances that cover today's 2m7f test.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Survivors Sister has posted just one win in her last five starts alongside a pulled up and two mid-field finishes, and 108 days off the track adds a fitness query; that third one start back offers a sliver of encouragement, and she has going experience to call on.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter among nine runners, she is likely to dictate at a sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 2m7f — a trip that rewards organised, unhurried leaders rather than those who blaze and fade. Behind her, Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Survivors Sister and Straight Home all want prominent positions, creating a congested chasing pack from the outset, with traffic danger most acute two to three fences out as the field compresses on the run to the home straight. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate in those front positions, and Cherry Red and Carried With Love — both natural prominent horses — are likely to find themselves shuffled further back than their preferred roles dictate, unable to get the jump on the bend. With a sustainable pace set by one front-runner and a cluttered mid-section, this shape favours a horse sitting in a genuine, uncrowded prominent berth just off the leader who can track through cleanly and strike from the second-last — making the organised close-prominent profile the most advantageous in this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock secures an uncontested lead and the prominent pack cancel each other out in traffic.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock sets a measured tempo on going that suits her — she has hit the frame in all three starts on similar conditions — and the congestion behind her means no rival travels smoothly enough to mount a coordinated challenge jumping two out; she simply extends.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Striker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one well-placed prominent horse tracks Affinity Rock cleanly and delivers a decisive jump at the second-last.
scenarios.body: Survivors Sister or Joya Del Mar — both proven at this course and going — sits in the slipstream while the chasing pack is bottled up, then travels into contention without interference and hits the front before the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent logjam causes interference two out and opens a gap for a hold-up horse to come through.
scenarios.body: Ad Caelum or Cooke's Lass, tracking behind the chaos, finds a run inside the final half mile as rivals check and balance; the longer stamina test at 2m7f on soft-ish ground aids those who stay widest and latest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock is pressured unexpectedly and the pace spikes, causing most of the field to wilt in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Only the two horses with the most economical race position — those who settled earliest and jumped most fluently — have enough fuel left in the tank at 2m7f on testing ground; this rewards exceptional jumping efficiency over late acceleration.

watchPoints.text: Affinity Rock's ability to dictate unopposed is the single most important factor — watch if any runner goes with her early, as contested pace over 2m7f on Good to Yielding would dramatically change the race shape and who benefits.

The four-runner prominent cluster (Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Survivors Sister, Straight Home) risks serious interference between the second-last and last — horses on the outside of that group could be forced wide at the worst moment.

Carried With Love's 222-day absence is a significant query; if she jumps hesitantly or loses her position early, she has very little scope to recover given her natural style is being compromised already by the race shape.

Cooke's Lass (364 days off) and Ad Caelum (two recent P finishes) both have fitness or form questions — if either moves with unusual fluency early, it signals the yard has them primed and they become live threats in the late-surge scenario.

Cherry Red's recent track record shows he can win on Good ground at shorter trips — watch his jumping in the early part of the race to gauge whether he's handling the conditions; a fluent round could see him travel better than his map position suggests.

runners_data.name: Three Tribes
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last two comparable-going starts yielded no wins and no places; at 56 days off and age nine, needs significant improvement and the redistribution into midfield reflects the crowded closer market rather than any tactical upgrade.
runners_data.comment: Three Tribes has pulled up in three of his last five starts and ranks 17th of 19 on our figures, making him very hard to fancy; he does have going experience and showed he can win, but that form feels distant against this company.

runners_data.name: Subset
runners_data.note: Lightly raced flag and 470-day absence is a serious concern; going profile unknown, and at age 12 returning from such a layoff this is speculative at best even on a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning from a 470-day absence, Subset faces a stiff ask on comeback — yet he has run over today's trip and going, and that second last time out hints at ability, with our rating of 95 suggesting he holds stronger claims than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio
runners_data.note: Martin Brassil's nine-year-old has won at 25f on soft and placed on good, carrying OR 100 as the highest-rated runner; at 38 days off and with a strong soft-or-good record (1W1P in two similar-going runs), this is a major player for the late-closing scenario.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has previous form on today's going, but our rating of 91 trails several rivals and 168 lb is a stern burden; the 38-day absence is a mild query for a gelding who has shown he can produce when ready.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who landed a recent win over 22f on good and returns on just 11 days' rest — trainer W J Lanigan going 1/3 over the fortnight; the step to 2m7f is untested but youth and freshness are selling points in a wide-open field.
runners_data.comment: Not So Serious boasts strong claims on our rating, ranked third of 19 runners, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; however, his recent form is erratic — a winner three starts back, he has since unseated and finished ninth in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's six-year-old is the Strand Scorecard top selection with outstanding going form (2W4P from eight similar-going starts) and back-to-back wins; Alan O'Sullivan (5lb) keeps the ride and the 22-day break looks ideal — the profile suits this race shape precisely.
runners_data.comment: Ladies Well arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, yet our rating of 91 sits seven pounds below her official mark and she carries 166 lb, which may test her stamina.

runners_data.name: Hit The Frame
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has failed to win any of four good-ground starts at this sort of trip; 118 days off is a stamina concern and the form figures (4,7,4) suggest he finds one or two too good at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Hit The Frame has failed to win in his last four starts and, ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, is hard to fancy; 118 days off the track adds another question mark, though he has distance and going experience and does own a win in recent form.

runners_data.name: Las Brisas Boy
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's five-year-old has placed twice from six attempts on good ground and ran well over shorter recently; prominent style suits if the pace is modest, but the step to 2m7f — a full 7f beyond his best — is a significant query.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter but winless in his last five starts, Las Brisas Boy has back-to-back runner-up finishes to his name and has experience of today's going, though a hefty 156 lb burden may test his resolve in a competitive nineteen-runner field.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's six-year-old has a solid going record (1W3P from ten similar-going starts) and is identified as a Strand danger; the hold-up style suits the likely race shape, though the last three efforts have been flat (6,6,3) and a return to winning form is needed.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out shows Mistyburn retains some ability, and he has run over today's distance and going before, but two consecutive sixths in the interim and a trainer striking at just 4% recently are harder to ignore under a hefty 157 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish tag and has shown no win or place in 11 comparable-going starts; nine-year-old's recent form (9,P,9,P,8) makes it hard to argue a case here at any price.
runners_data.comment: Tomas O Maille steps back up sharply in our ratings, topping the 19-runner field, and his third last time out — his best recent effort — suggests he retains ability; yet to score in his last six starts, though 14 days is a sharp enough turnaround and the distance and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: Has won and placed on soft/good and landed a recent victory at 24f; no jockey named which is a notable concern in a 19-runner handicap chase — connections management worth monitoring before committing.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and fourth two starts back, Island McCoo's recent form is modest, though a win four starts back shows he can find the winner's enclosure; he has distance and going experience to call on, but 157 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Swing Time
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose true closing style is compressed by the crowded rear group; recent form (6 on soft, three finishes of 5,8,8 on good) is uninspiring and the redistribution into midfield reduces any late-run advantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up two runs back, Swing Time faces a stiff ask off 146 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 87 suggests connections may still believe there is more to come.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old with a remarkable 12-start record on similar going (3W7P) and in-form recently (1,3,2,1,1,2); Sarah Kavanagh (7) takes the ride for John Carr whose yard is 0/3 in the last fortnight, but the horse's own record is the standout in this field for a prominent scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ranked a long way below the assessments of his rivals on our figures, Fr Gilligansvoyge is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 158 lb, yet his recent form reads well with three wins in his last six starts and a second last time out.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner but carries a fades-in-finish flag; 11-year-old with recent P,P finishes and only a modest going record (1W2P from nine), making it likely he sets the race up for others rather than winning it himself.
runners_data.comment: Kilashee has struggled badly in her last two starts, pulling up on both occasions, and remains winless in recent starts, so there are obvious concerns; yet she has run over today's distance and going before, and our rating of 93 suggests she retains more ability than her official mark of 80 implies.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Good-ground form reads well (1W3P from nine similar-going starts) and he has won over the trip; a genuine hold-up horse repositioned into midfield by the crowded market — the style-fit discount (0.93) tempers expectations but he is not without claims if the race falls right.
runners_data.comment: Set The Tone shaped well enough when runner-up last time out, but a sixth two starts back and a pulled-up effort in recent starts make her hard to fancy at the foot of the rankings, and 145 lb is a stiff ask despite her familiarity with today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's eight-year-old has two wins on good ground but recent form has faded (0, then 4th two back); a 21-day turnaround and a tendency to run well fresh could spark revival, though last outing was a disappointing zero.
runners_data.comment: Zolpharine has back-to-back wins three and four starts back, but two disappointing efforts since, including an unplaced run last time out, and our figures rank him well adrift of this field carrying 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Walkmethroughit
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose last seven comparative runs have produced no wins and no places; headgear noted, 49 days off, and the form figures (7,P,P,7,7) make a compelling case to oppose rather than support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last of 19 on our figures, Walkmethroughit's recent form — two pull-ups sandwiched between a string of sevenths — makes him extremely difficult to fancy, though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 49-day break.

runners_data.name: Reve Inoui
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 97 days off for J P Flavin; recent form (8,4,5) over similar trips and going is moderate and the layoff introduces fitness risk, though Jordan Canavan (7) on board keeps the weight manageable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 97 days off, Reve Inoui nevertheless catches the eye on our rating of 98, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions — the concern is whether that lengthy absence blunts his edge against a deep field.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old owned in the John Patrick Ryan yard returning just four days after his last run — the very short turnaround merits scrutiny; a natural hold-up horse bumped into midfield by the crowded rear group, and form figures (0,3,3,7,P) suggest he needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: The Little Yank shaped with promise when third in consecutive starts, and his rating of 100 gives him a strong claim as a leading threat carrying 154 lb; the concern is he arrives just four days after his last run, winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Carries both a fades-in-finish tag and the redistribution flag; five starts on similar going have produced zero wins and zero places, and the combination of those factors alongside an absence of a jockey listing makes this a very difficult horse to support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 19 here, U Asking Me does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and returns on a reasonable 28-day break, though a fall last time and a pulled-up finish among his recent outings give obvious cause for caution.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, critically, carries a fades-in-finish flag — meaning he is likely to set a genuine but ultimately unsustainable gallop over this 2m7f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. With no serious challenger likely to press him hard from the off, the early pace should be honest rather than frantic, producing a steadily-run race that will nevertheless stretch the field on the final circuit. Fr Gilligansvoyge, Las Brisas Boy, Hit The Frame and Reve Inoui are the prominent types most likely to sit just off Kilashee and dictate terms from the front rank, while the large hold-up cohort — including Ladies Well, Mistyburn and Il Silenzio — will need the race to develop into a true test of stamina in the closing stages. The field contains significantly more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Three Tribes, Swing Time, The Little Yank, U Asking Me and Set The Tone are all genuine closers pushed into the midfield projection, and in practice those horses will be competing for a narrower late-running opportunity than they would ideally want. This race shape — a lone front-runner who is likely to fade, moderate early pace, strong finish — firmly favours hold-up and staying types who can travel kindly and arrive with momentum in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee's pace proves sustainable enough to string the field out but ultimately fades in the final quarter-mile, releasing a wave of closers.
scenarios.body: Ladies Well's profile — six from eight on similar going, in career-best form and ridden patiently — is perfectly tailored to this shape, and Mistyburn and Il Silenzio have the staying credentials and good-ground form to deliver late challenges at this extreme trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Persist
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely modest and front-rankers conserve enough energy to resist the closers through the final two fences.
scenarios.body: Fr Gilligansvoyge's extraordinary recent record — three wins and seven places from twelve on similar going — makes him the outstanding beneficiary if the race is run at a pace that rewards those who travel prominently throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Yielding ground rides more testing than reported and the race becomes a war of attrition from three out.
scenarios.body: Il Silenzio has won over 25f on soft and placed on good, and at OR 100 carries real class over the redistributed hold-up types forced out of their natural position; Mistyburn's 10 from 14 on similar going also reads well in a pure stamina scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Improvers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the race is so muddling that midfield types find clear daylight and arrive at the right time without ever being buried in the traffic.
scenarios.body: Set The Tone's 1W3P on good ground from a prominent-to-midfield position gives him an outside claim, and Not So Serious has the freshness of an 11-day turnaround with a recent win at this sort of trip; however, both horses are racing at least partly out of their preferred role which tempers confidence significantly.

watchPoints.text: Ladies Well's jumping — Alan O'Sullivan (5) has to navigate a 19-runner field and any jumping error in a bunched mid-race group could end what looks a strong chance on form.

Fr Gilligansvoyge at age 13 — monitor market moves and any late market drift that might signal the trainer has concerns despite the horse's outstanding recent record at this course and trip combination.
Kilashee's early jumping — as the lone front-runner with a fades-in-finish flag, any blunder at an early fence could disrupt the entire field's positioning and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Island McCoo has no jockey listed — a confirmed rider and market move closer to post time would significantly increase the case for including this horse whose form figures and going record are genuinely competitive.

The Little Yank runs just four days after his last outing for the busy John Patrick Ryan yard (2/14 in 14 days); if he shows signs of below-par preparation in the market, the short turnaround warrants significant weight in any assessment.
